cards.explanation: The answer is False. The text says the crowds found out about it and followed Him on foot from the towns (Matthew 14:13). Jesus went by boat, and they went by foot, friends. I've chased a cookie box across a counter before, but this is next level.

The answer is that He has compassion on them. When He stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them (Matthew 14:14). He went looking for a solitary place and found a crowd instead. I think a lot of us would've sighed, friends, but the text says compassion.

The answer is heals. Jesus saw the large crowd, had compassion on them, and healed their sick (Matthew 14:14). Look at the order there, friends. The compassion came first, and the healing followed right behind it.

The answer is to send them to the villages to buy food. The disciples said, “Dismiss the crowds so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food.” (Matthew 14:15) They'd looked at the late hour and the desolate place and came up with a plan, friends. I think it was a practical one.

The answer is the disciples. Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” (Matthew 14:16) He had just said the crowds did not need to go away, and then He handed the job right back to the disciples. I bet they did a double take, friends.

The answer is only five loaves and two fish. The disciples answered, “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish…” (Matthew 14:17) Notice that word “only,” friends. I bet that's the sound of someone who did the math and doesn't love the result.

The answer is True. Matthew says Jesus directed the crowds to sit down on the grass, and then He took the loaves and the fish (Matthew 14:19). That direction came before a single piece of bread went out, friends. It's like clearing the counter before the baking starts.

The answer is heaven. Jesus took the loaves and the fish, looked up to heaven, and spoke a blessing (Matthew 14:19). The blessing came before He broke the loaves and gave them out, friends. That's a good habit for any kitchen.

The answer is ate and satisfied. The text says, “They all ate and were satisfied…” (Matthew 14:20). All of them ate, friends, not just the front rows. Not just fed, but satisfied. I've served plenty of cookies, and that's the review I dream about.

The answer is twelve basketfuls. The disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over (Matthew 14:20). They started with five loaves and two fish and ended with twelve baskets, friends. I need to sit down.

The answer is True. The text says, “About five thousand men were fed, besides women and children.” (Matthew 14:21) The women and children are in addition to the five thousand, friends. So the real crowd was bigger than that number.
